subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Tunnel Boring Machines: Underground Giants
description: One-minute skill: Tunnel Boring Machines: Underground Giants.

hook.text: The largest tunnel boring machine ever built was 57 feet in diameter. It weighed 7,000 tons and was named Bertha.

buildup.text: A TBM cuts rock with a rotating head studded with disc cutters. Behind the head, it installs prefabricated concrete segments.

discovery.text: The machine pushes forward by gripping the lining with hydraulic jacks. It moves about 50 feet per day through hard rock.

twist.text: Bertha got stuck under Seattle for two years. A steel pipe left in the ground from a test well jammed the cutter head.

climax.text: Modern TBMs include sensors that detect ground conditions ahead. Some can switch between rock-cutting and soft-ground modes.

punchline.text: 57 feet wide. 7,000 tons. Stuck by a forgotten pipe.

quiz.question: What caused the TBM Bertha to get stuck under Seattle for two years?
options: Unexpected volcanic rock was harder than the cutter head could handle
A steel pipe left from a test well jammed the cutter head underground
Groundwater flooding overwhelmed the machine's pumping capacity
